newsitem.title: USA: Xerox launches first product for the home.
newsitem.headline: Xerox launches first product for the home.

text.p: Photocopier giant Xerox Corp., a long-time leader in corporate copiers, Monday unveiled its first product for the home, a $499 combination printer, copier and scanner for personal computers.
Dubbed the Document HomeCentre, the device is aimed at small and home offices, Xerox said.
The company also introduced the Document WorkCentre 450c, a device that combines color printing with faxing, copying and scanning and has a retail price of $549.

With its new products, the Stamford, Conn.-based company -- long synonymous with photocopying equipment for the large corporate market -- is entering a market now dominated by companies like Hewlett-Packard Co. and Japan's Canon Inc.

The company said the new devices are the first Xerox products that use color inkjet technology developed at its Webster, N.Y.-based Wilson Research Center. The scanning and document management software technologies that are part of the products originate at its Palo Alto Research Center, it said.

The Document HomeCentre will be available at stores in the United States and Canada early next month, Xerox said. It will be available in Europe in the fourth quarter of this year and Latin America in the first quarter of 1998.
The Document WorkCentre 450c will be available at U.S. and Canadian retailers later this month, and will be in Europe and Latin America in the fourth quarter of this year.
Xerox stock dipped 12.5 cents to $74.625 in consolidated morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
